driver_package.oem_note: the INF banner ends in -HP and was published by the Microsoft Windows Hardware Compatibility Publisher, i.e. it is an HP-packaged OEM driver rather than a retail AMD Adrenalin installer

documented_requirement.statement: the published page states a Windows ML minimum and an Adrenalin minimum; it states no gfx/DID list, so gfx1151 eligibility cannot be read from it

adrenalin_software_version.reason: the installed AMD software package reports 10.25.20179.0 and the INF banner reports the driver-package build 25.20.18; neither is the Adrenalin marketing version and no documented mapping exists, so the documented Adrenalin minimum can be neither confirmed nor refuted from read-only telemetry
adrenalin_software_version.corroboration_only: the driver date 2025-09-17 is later than the Adrenalin 24.12.1 release window; this is consistent with, not proof of, meeting the minimum

compatibility_findings.statement: OS build 26200.9974 satisfies the documented 24H2 (26100+) requirement
Windows ML binding 2.5.96 satisfies the documented 2.5.96 minimum

compatibility_findings.why: no documented mapping from 32.0.22018.5 or 25.20.18 to an Adrenalin marketing version

compatibility_findings.statement: gfx1151 / DID 0x1586 explicitly supported by AMDGPU EP
compatibility_findings.why: no official gfx/DID list is published; cannot be tested without the EP

compatibility_findings.statement: the installed display driver can run GPU inference at all
compatibility_findings.why: the DirectML canary executes on this adapter with positive DML profiler nodes

compatibility_findings.statement: HP OEM packaging blocks the AMDGPU EP
compatibility_findings.why: no official statement ties the AMDGPU EP to a retail AMD installer

verdict: DRIVER_REQUIREMENT_NEITHER_PROVEN_NOR_REFUTED; the driver stack is functional for DirectML and no evidence ties the empty catalog to the HP OEM driver
